question: Should OpenClaw browser page navigation make HTTP(S) URLs with embedded username/password userinfo unsupported and fail fast before any browser or proxy dispatch?
rationale: The security hardening reduces credential exposure, but it intentionally breaks URL-embedded Basic-auth navigation workflows and needs an explicit maintainer policy choice before merge.

options.title: Fail fast and redact
options.body: Reject credentialed browser navigation URLs before dispatch, redact malformed credential-like diagnostics, and direct users to authenticated profiles, cookies, headers, or Playwright credentials.

options.title: Preserve Basic-auth URLs with stronger redaction
options.body: Keep URL-embedded credentials working but improve log/error redaction, accepting that raw credential-bearing URLs still reach the browser runtime.

options.title: Defer to browser auth design
options.body: Pause this PR until maintainers define a broader browser authentication alternative and compatibility story.

recommendation.title: Fail fast and redact
recommendation.body: Reject credentialed browser navigation URLs before dispatch, redact malformed credential-like diagnostics, and direct users to authenticated profiles, cookies, headers, or Playwright credentials.

likelyOwner.reason: The inspected history and current assignment make steipete the clearest owner for the browser plugin policy and compatibility decision.
